## Function

NAIP proteins recognize bacterial flagellin or type-III secretion-system components and recruit NLRC4 to assemble an inflammasome. Caspase-1 activation then promotes IL-1-family cytokine maturation and pyroptotic defense.

::: {.gene-mechanism}
::: {.gene-state}
**NAIP–NLRC4 intact**

Invasive bacterial structures can trigger rapid epithelial/innate defense.
:::
::: {.gene-flow-arrow}
→
:::
::: {.gene-state .gene-state-off}
**NLRC4 lost**

Defense against relevant pathogens may weaken; excessive inflammatory injury may also fall.
:::
:::

NLRC4 and NLRP3 are not redundant synonyms: their upstream triggers differ. Hypomethylation in severe UC may mark immune-cell abundance or regulatory change, but it does not demonstrate inflammasome activity.

## What is distinctive about NLRC4

NAIPs provide ligand recognition and nucleate NLRC4 oligomerization; bacterial flagellin and type-III-secretion-system proteins are canonical triggers. Reactome curates this neighborhood as the IPAF inflammasome [@milacic2024reactome]. The response can rapidly activate caspase-1 and expel or kill infected cells. Human and mouse NAIP repertoires differ, so ligand specificity cannot always be transferred directly between species.

## Relevance and evidence gap in UC

NLRC4 is biologically plausible where barrier breach increases bacterial access, but a severe-UC DMR does not identify ligand, assembled complex, or cellular source. Demonstrating the pathway requires sensor-specific stimulation or complex capture alongside cleaved caspase-1, gasdermin D, IL-18/IL-1β, and epithelial versus myeloid localization. Without those measurements, the locus is an inflammatory-context marker.

<details><summary><strong>Interpret with NLRP3, not as NLRP3</strong></summary>

Measure sensor-specific triggers and complexes, caspase-1 products, pyroptosis, and cellular origin. A shared downstream cytokine is not proof of which inflammasome fired.
</details>
